A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaRI research, with matching methods and shared experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes Appendix A.1–A.6, which was included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSO and SCRREAM reconstruction experiments, efficiency measurements, and layer-count, pretraining and mask-prediction ablations in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original reconstruction experiments and adds 3D-FRONT evaluation, further comparisons and appendix ablations in Tables 2–10.

M1.justification: Both versions use layered point maps, separate point-map and ray-stopping networks, scale-shift-aligned geometric supervision and cross-entropy stopping-index supervision. v2 explicitly describes per-layer prediction heads and tests alternative architectures and outputs, but does not establish a change to the proposed default method.

E1.justification: v2 adds quantitative evaluation on held-out synthetic indoor scenes from 3D-FRONT, previously used only for training, and qualitative evaluation on non-training ScanNet++ images. The object and indoor-scene tasks, training sources, and GSO/SCRREAM benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The GSO view-aligned comparison expands from SF3D, SPAR3D and TRELLIS in v1 Table 1 to also include DUSt3R, VGGT and MoGe in v2 Table 2. This adds a distinct geometric-foundation-model comparator group to a central experiment. The original object baselines and quantitative scene comparator set are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a disjoint 2,300-image 3D-FRONT test subset, filtered for at least 30% unseen pixels, and additional experimental configurations for the new ablations. Efficiency evaluation now also includes both networks together, while the separately reported fixed-sampling Ours* setting disappears. Existing training hyperparameters and GSO/SCRREAM point-sampling budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds DINOv3 pretraining, shared-versus-separate encoders, per-layer reconstruction accuracy, and point-map-versus-depth-plus-focal-length ablations, plus layer-coverage analysis in Figure 6. These address previously untested design choices and occlusion behavior. Existing layer-count and mask-strategy ablations remain; the Ours* sampling comparison is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new dataset statistics and layer-coverage plots do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Shared GSO and SCRREAM benchmark scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial result sets for 3D-FRONT, new object baselines and appendix analyses. For example, LaRI's new 3D-FRONT overall results are CD 0.061 and FS@0.05 0.799. Table 6 adds combined-network measurements of 620.2M parameters and 51.5 ms; these measure a broader system than the retained point-map-only results. Ours* and some scene F-score entries disappear. Table 8's dataset attribution is unclear: its text names SCRREAM, but its separate-encoder scores match the GSO baseline.

T1.justification: The representation, alignment loss and stopping-index mathematics are substantively unchanged. v2's head/concatenation equations and standard Chamfer-distance and F-score formulas explain existing procedures. No new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 removes the prominent claim of matching TRELLIS with 4% of its training data and 17% of its parameters, retaining a broader efficiency claim. It emphasizes fully supervised prediction and annotations for five datasets. The central contribution—single-view, feed-forward, view-aligned reconstruction of visible and occluded geometry across objects and scenes—remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of design choices: it attributes shared-encoder degradation to task competition, depth-output degradation to focal-length ambiguity, and deeper-layer errors to reduced context. It also qualifies full-system efficiency relative to MoGe, explicitly discusses synthetic-to-real domain gaps, and explains why incomplete ScanNet++ geometry limits quantitative evaluation.

D1.justification: Beyond relocating existing annotation descriptions, v2 supplies camera-axis conventions, rotation-transposition requirements, per-layer head details, ground-truth sampling sources, ten-layer scene ground truth, and 1,000 rotation candidates for registration. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changes to the underlying retained experiments. The project link and promised pipeline release remain; v1's explicit promise to release evaluation data and scripts is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of close work, including DRDF, MLD, Rayst3R, X-ray, Flash3D and Splatter Image, and cites VGGT and DINOv3. It more explicitly acknowledges LDI inspiration and distinguishes geometric supervision from photorealistic view synthesis. These refine positioning within the existing related-work framework; publication updates to retained references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and substantial related-work and evaluation passages are rewritten. Data construction is condensed in the main text and moved into an expanded appendix, implementation explanations are reorganized, conclusions precede limitations, and an Impact Statement is added. This is substantial editorial restructuring despite the stable core method.

P2.justification: v2 adds quantitative panels to Figure 1, redesigns object and scene comparisons with multiple views, and adds coverage plots and appendix visualizations. Tables gain dataset statistics, additional comparator rows, a two-dataset scene layout, combined-network efficiency rows and new ablation displays. Conference formatting, captions, shading and placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the evidence and transparency supporting LaRI. New design and per-layer analyses address previously untested choices, while detailed rendering and registration instructions improve reproducibility. Crucially, Table 6 reports the stopping-index network's additional cost and qualifies the efficiency advantage, correcting the incomplete accounting in v1's point-map-only comparison. Table 8's unclear dataset attribution and removal of the sampling comparison limit parts of the revision, but do not outweigh these substantive gains.
